newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 17.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--European Union leaders made a symbolic U-turn towards a "social Europe" at Amsterdam yesterday with the French-German spat being resolved with a compromise. The Greek side says it is satisfied with developments.
--In Athens, Defence Minister and leading ruling PASOK party member Akis Tsohatzopoulos says the emphasis on economic stability has resulted in social and development policies lagging behind.
--Dimitra Liani-Papandreou reveals what happened on the night Andreas Papandreou, the late founder and president of ruling PASOK, succumbed to his long illness.
--Turkey has threatened to send its forces to the region of Imia, the islet at the centre of a dispute between Athens and Ankara last year, to investigate claims of Greek vessels in the area.
--A recent Supreme Court ruling has opened the way for a return of significant amounts of compound interest collected by banks from firms.
--Greek athetes at the Mediterranean Games have brought 11 gold and three records in the first three days of the games. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
